verses.text: The Pharisees and some legal experts who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus.
They noticed that some of his disciples ate with hands considered unclean—that is, without washing them first.
The Pharisees and all the Jews followed the elders’ tradition and wouldn’t eat without carefully washing their hands.
When they came from the marketplace, they wouldn’t eat without washing. They also observed many other traditions, such as washing cups, pitchers, bronze pots, and dining couches.
So the Pharisees and legal experts asked Jesus, “Why don’t your disciples follow the elders’ tradition? They’re eating with unwashed hands!”
He replied, “Isaiah was right when he prophesied about you hypocrites. As Scripture says: ‘These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
Their worship of me is pointless; their teachings are just human rules.’
You let go of God’s command and cling to human traditions—you wash pitchers and cups, and do many similar things.”
Then he said, “You’re very good at setting aside God’s command so you can keep your tradition!
Moses said, ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Anyone who curses their father or mother must be put to death.’
But you say that if someone tells their father or mother, ‘Whatever help you might have received from me is Corban’—that is, dedicated to God—
then you no longer let them do anything for their father or mother.
In this way you cancel God’s word through the tradition you’ve passed down. And you do many things like this.”
Jesus called the crowd back and said, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
Nothing outside a person that goes into them can make them unclean. What comes out of a person is what makes them unclean.
Anyone who has ears to hear should listen.”
When Jesus went inside away from the crowd, his disciples asked him about the teaching.
He said, “Are you still missing it? Don’t you understand that nothing from outside can make a person unclean
by going into them? It doesn’t enter their heart, but their stomach, and then it goes out of the body.” In saying this, Jesus declared all foods clean.
He continued, “What comes out of a person is what makes them unclean.
For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder,
adultery, greed, wickedness, deceit, shamelessness, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.
All these evils come from within and make a person unclean.”
Jesus left that area and went to the region of Tyre. He entered a house and didn’t want anyone to know he was there, but he couldn’t stay hidden.
A woman whose little daughter had an impure spirit heard about him. She came and fell at his feet.
The woman was Greek, born in Syrian Phoenicia, and she begged Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
He said to her, “First let the children eat all they want. It isn’t right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
She replied, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
Then he told her, “Because you said that, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”
She went home and found her child lying on the bed, with the demon gone.
Jesus left the region of Tyre, traveled through Sidon, and went to the Sea of Galilee and the region of the Decapolis.
Some people brought him a man who was deaf and could barely speak. They begged Jesus to place his hand on him.
Jesus took him away from the crowd, put his fingers in the man’s ears, and touched his tongue with spit.
He looked up to heaven, sighed, and said, “Ephphatha!”—which means, “Be opened!”
At once the man’s ears were opened, his tongue was freed, and he began speaking clearly.
Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more he ordered them, the more widely they spread the news.
People were completely amazed and said, “He’s done everything well! He even makes deaf people hear and people who can’t speak talk!”
